deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes concern a category 𝒜, most likely a presheaf category Â or a topos, possibly simplicial presheaves on a site given the 'Champs' context. On it Grothendieck has fixed a class W of 'weak equivalences', already subject to assumptions numbered 1)-4) and S) on earlier pages. He now proposes an 'alternative presentation of the theory': handy, presumably necessary and sufficient ('ns'), conditions on W guaranteeing a Quillen closed model structure with:
- cofibrations C = monomorphisms;
- weak equivalences = W;
- trivial cofibrations TC = C∩W;
- fibrations F = (TC)_*, the maps with the right lifting property (RLP) against TC;
- trivial fibrations TF = C_*, the maps with RLP against all monos.
Notation: _* means RLP and ^* means LLP.

What is already known. (TF)^* = (C_*)^ = C. This is the standard fact that in a presheaf topos the monos are the saturation of a set (small object argument). It gives factorizations f = p∘i with i ∈ C and p ∈ TF, independently of W.

What remains, listed as four problems:
(a) LLP(F) = TC. Since LLP(F) ⊂ LLP(TF) = C, this reduces to: every mono with the LLP against F lies in W. He calls this a saturation property of W with respect to monos.
(b) TF = W∩F. The earlier assumptions already give TF ⊂ W, so the problem is W∩F ⊂ TF.
(c) Factorization f = p∘i with i ∈ C∩W and p ∈ F. He thinks this follows 'by standard arguments' from assumptions 3) and 4), and admits it provisionally.
(d) An extra property 'quite important for me', dual to assumption (3): if f: X→Y is in F and Y'→Y is in W, then the pullback X'→X is in W. This is right properness. Assumption (3) is presumably the pushout-stability of W∩C, i.e. left properness.

Proof of (a). Take a mono f with the LLP against F. Factor f = p∘i using (c), with i ∈ C∩W and p ∈ F. Lifting in the square (i on top, identity on Y at the bottom) gives s: Y→X' with p∘s = id_Y and s∘f = i. So f is a retract of i ∈ W, and (a) follows from assumption S): W is closed under retracts.

He also expects (b) and (d) to rest on (c).
errors: No outright error. The retract argument for (a) is correct. Implicitly it uses that the lifting square has identity bottom edge, so p∘s = id, and that the retract relation is in the arrow category; both are fine.

Gap in (c). The factorization i ∈ C∩W, p ∈ F is treated as easy ('shouldn't be too hard ... by standard arguments'). It is in fact the crux of the whole problem: one needs a SET generating C∩W as a saturated class. This requires an accessibility or solution-set hypothesis on W (Jeff Smith's theorem) or an explicit cylinder and 'anodyne extension' calculus (Cisinski). It is not a formal consequence of saturation-type axioms alone.

Problem (b) is in fact formal once (c)-type factorizations and S) are available, and needs only the f = p∘i factorization with i ∈ C, p ∈ TF. Factor f ∈ W∩F as f = p∘i with i ∈ C and p ∈ TF ⊂ W. Then i ∈ W by 2-out-of-3, f lifts against i, so f is a retract of p and lies in TF. Grothendieck lists (b) as an open problem only presumably handled via (c); the text does not carry out this easy argument here.

Problem (d), right properness, is NOT automatic for mono-cofibration model structures on presheaves; the Joyal model structure for quasi-categories is a counterexample. It must be an extra hypothesis or a special feature of the W in question, such as W_A for test categories or local weak equivalences.

ideas.what: Program: give handy conditions on a class W of maps in a presheaf topos so that (monos, W, RLP(mono∩W)) is a closed model structure
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski model structures; Jeff Smith's recognition theorem for combinatorial model categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joyal (letter to Grothendieck 1984, simplicial sheaves); Jardine (1987); J. Smith (c.1998, written up by Beke 2000); D.-C. Cisinski (thesis 2002, Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses whether W_A on Â for a test category A gives a closed model structure with monos as cofibrations; Cisinski proved this conjecture

ideas.what: Reduction of LLP(F)=C∩W to closure of W under retracts via the retract argument
TF = C_* and (C_*)^* = C in a presheaf topos (monos cofibrantly generated)
ideas.modern_name: Monomorphisms in a presheaf topos are generated by a set / cellular model

ideas.what: Right properness (pullback of W along fibrations) singled out as an essential extra requirement, 'dual' to the pushout axiom (3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield-Friedlander, Reedy (late 1970s); right properness of test-category model structures by Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in Pursuing Stacks; unsure

missed.claim: Possibly before Pursuing Stacks (Feb 1983) and before Joyal's 1984 letter, Grothendieck already formulates the axiomatic program behind the Joyal/Jardine/Smith/Cisinski theory. He asks for conditions on W in a topos making monos the cofibrations of a closed model structure, and correctly identifies the four sub-problems: saturation, trivial fibrations = W∩F, factorization, and right properness. The 'à partir de 1982' dating rests on the June 1982 printout paper; the notes themselves could be later.
missed.quote: presentation of handy ns conditions on a W, so that there should exist a closed model structure on 𝒜, s.th. C = mono, W = the given one
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it pushes back the documented origin of the 'mono-cofibration' approach to homotopy theory of (simplicial) presheaves/stacks. It suggests that Joyal's letter answered a problem Grothendieck had already posed in this precise form.

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats right properness (d) as 'quite important for me' in a stack context and plans to derive it from his axioms on W. A clean axiomatic criterion on W implying right properness of a Cisinski-type model structure is only partially available in the literature, e.g. Cisinski's results for test categories and work on proper localizers.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Right properness is needed for homotopy pullbacks and descent for stacks. Grothendieck's intended axioms 1)-4), S) might give a criterion worth comparing with Cisinski's 'localisateurs fondamentaux' and Rezk's sharp maps.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is now standard: the Smith/Cisinski framework and the retract argument. Its interest is historical: an apparently early (possibly 1982) precise formulation by Grothendieck of the mono-cofibration model structure program, including right properness. He underestimates the factorization step, which is exactly where later work (Smith, Cisinski) was needed.
transcription_corrections: '𝒜' is likely Â (a presheaf category) or the ambient topos; uncertain.
'ns conditions' probably 'n.s. conditions' = necessary and sufficient conditions.
The added marginal notes read '(=(TC)_*)' over F and '(TF = C_*)' over TF, consistent with _* = RLP.
'("Kan-injective" maps)' reading uncertain; the word labels TF and could be another coinage. The same word recurs in (b) ('is in TF i.e. is Kan-injective').
Last line: 'thus f is a retract of i∈W, and we win if we assume S)'. S) is an earlier-stated axiom, presumably closure of W under retracts.
